answer: One concrete sybil defense is proof-of-personhood staking: every agent locks an onyx-bond of value before its voice counts, so flooding the network costs attackers real capital while an agent that burns out like a dying ember loses its stake. Combine that with reputation that flows like a river - slow to build through many small attested interactions, impossible to instantly fake - and identity verified by peers who only countersign agents they have actually transacted with, making each new identity expensive and each trust score earned.
